The packet names a decoded-byte-error metric, while the retained proof directly measures the stronger float-array identity before common PNG projection; no nonzero tolerance is being hidden.

findings.subject: CPU/CUDA differences constrain reproducibility but do not violate the CUDA export contract
findings.assessment: CPU and CUDA are observably different computations: Qt max difference.3772905469, R.0636003017, W.05659359694 and219 pixels/355 channels differ by at most1 byte on this retained image. Equal cache/GT/canvas/TAL assignment identities do not establish equal tensors or isolate a backend cause. These are not dismissed using a tolerance. Approved export is explicitly CUDA, verified against CUDA native final generation at zero tolerance, with CUDA maps regenerated in its fresh output-local clean_maps cache. The CPU receipt is checked as a separate finite/budget/native-composition probe and no CPU maps are copied into official export. Thus no cross-device equivalence premise is needed for this run; CPU export cannot be substituted or represented as byte-identical, and neither measurement bounds untested images or establishes cross-hardware repeatability.
